topic: The Physics of Refraction: Why Light Bends

sections.title: The Hook: The Broken Pencil Illusion
lecture_lines: A pencil in water looks broken.
Light bends at the air-water interface.
This is the phenomenon of refraction.
animations: Create a pencil object in center screen #FFFFFF, Label it "Pencil".
Create a glass of water, label "Water" #00BFFF.
Move pencil partially into the water, visually offset it.
Fade in text "Refraction" #FFD700 near the bend.
Highlight the bend area with a glowing circle #FF4500.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Speed of Light in Media
lecture_lines: The refractive index measures light speed.
Light slows down in denser media.
This speed change causes light to bend.
animations: Display light ray in vacuum #FFFFFF, label "Speed c".
Display light ray in water, label "Speed v" #00BFFF.
Show light speed v being slower than c.

sections.title: Snell’s Law: The Mathematical Geometry
lecture_lines: Snell’s Law calculates the bending angle.
It uses indices and sine values.
The normal line is our reference.
Compare the incident and refractive angles.
Geometry predicts the path of light.
animations: Draw two media layers, air #F0F8FF and water #00BFFF.
Draw normal line to the boundary #808080.
Show equation: n1 sin(θ1) = n2 sin(θ2) #FFFFFF.

sections.title: Visualizing Direction: Toward or Away from Normal
lecture_lines: Moving to denser media, light bends inward.
Moving to lighter media, light bends outward.
Always measure angles from the normal line.
animations: Draw light entering denser medium, show bending towards normal.
Draw light entering thinner medium, show bending away normal.
Highlight angle change with arc markers #FF4500.

sections.title: Application: The Archer Fish
lecture_lines: The archer fish hunts insects above.
Refraction shifts the bug’s apparent position.
The fish adjusts its aim to strike.
animations: Draw archer fish underwater #00BFFF looking up.
Show light ray bending at surface, illustrating optical illusion.
